# MD-C8 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/MD-C8.txt; _text/MD-C8_paged.txt adds PDF page markers and _text/lined.txt is a line index used for searching. Page references give the report pagination first and the PDF page in brackets (roman vii-xx = PDF 10-23; arabic n = PDF n+23).

Scope: headline claims = executive summary (p.vii-xx, PDF 10-23) and Chapter 10 Conclusion (p.149-151, PDF 172-174). The executive summary "Conclusion" subsection and Chapter 10 are almost word-for-word the same; each claim is registered once, with both locations. Chapter 10 adds two claims (C104 pandemic paragraph, C129 personal budgets as standard practice). Background, funding and methods paragraphs of the executive summary were not registered as claims. Chapter conclusions (3.3, 4.4, 5.3, 6.7, 7.8, 8.10, 9.3) were not treated as headline locations; the executive summary repeats them almost verbatim.

## Rows proposed
- findings: 80 (Q 61, N 19). transformations: 2. claims: 133. relations: 50 (covers 39, backs 11, clashes 0). decisions: header only.
- Joint claims (Q and N roots after tracing transformations): C27, C94, C97.
- 21 claims have empty rests_on (summary claims under rule 2, framing statements, or recommendations without a cited finding).
- F7 (98% social housing) and F19 (progress toward tenancy targets) are main reported results that no registered headline claim rests on.

## Look at first
1. C94 (police and criminal justice costs rose for n=21; fit discord). The executive summary states the N result and in the same sentence says it departs "from interviewee accounts regarding overall trends" (p.xviii; s.9.2.2 p.141). rests_on F16 (N) and F28 (Q). This is the only explicit discord between the strands in the report.
2. C23 (interviewees perceived a downward trend in criminal activity, Q) and C94. No 'clashes' relation is proposed. The authors explain both can hold (small sample, one individual inflates the figures), so under rule 4 this is a qualification, not a clash. A1 may judge otherwise.
3. C93 (shift in health service use, n=21). rests_on F15 (N) only. Results section 9.2.2 (p.141) says these figures "are more congruent with the qualitative interview evidence regarding outcomes reported in s.5.2", but neither the executive summary nor 9.3 cites the interview evidence for this claim. Under rule 3 the Q link is left out of rests_on. If A1 accepts the results-section link, C93 becomes joint (fit confirm with F24).
4. C27 (outcomes catalysed a growing consensus that Housing First works). rests_on F8 (N, sustainment) with F31 and F32 (Q, interviews). The basis is s.5.1.1 p.50: "This outcome, combined with the other achievements [...] had led to a general shift in mindset". Proposed fit: expand (N gives the outcome, Q gives the stakeholder reading of it). Alternative: rests_on only F31/F32, with C13 backs C27 (R7) carrying the link. That choice decides whether C27 is joint.
5. C97 (positive trends in the small quantitative sample and, "taking the evaluation's qualitative findings into account also", potential for benefits to exceed costs). The text names the qualitative findings only in general terms. rests_on lists F15, F17 (N) and the main Q outcome findings F24, F25, F28. A1 should check whether a generic reference to "qualitative findings" is enough for rule 3.
6. C1 (fidelity high or high/medium). It rests on F18, the high/medium/low ratings, which T1 builds from wave one interview evidence (F20) ("It qualitatively assessed the Pathfinders' adherence to each principle (as either high, medium, or low)", p.4). T1 is recorded as crossing strands (Q to ordinal rating). Traced to roots, C1 is Q only, so it is not joint. Alternative: treat the ratings as Q and drop T1.
7. T2: the four costed case studies (F17) are N survey data written up as narrative; recorded as not crossing strands. Alternative: treat the narrative case studies as Q, which would make C95 Q-rooted through a crossing transformation.
8. Rule 1 splits not made: C26 (list of pandemic effects), C33 (five features), C120 (facilitators) and C121 (inhibitors) are each kept as one claim. All parts rest on the same finding (C26, C33) or are list summaries (C120, C121). Splitting would not change the joint count but would add 4 + 8 + 9 rows.
9. Summary claims under rule 2 (empty rests_on, linked by covers): C18, C96, C101-C105, C108, C112, C113, C120, C121. C18 cites "interviewees" as the source but no finding at that point; borderline.
10. Restatements: C99/C7, C100/C13-C14, C107/C46, C123/C56, C124/C82. Where the conclusion claim cites a figure (C99, C100) rests_on is given; R39 links C123 to C56 and R48 links C124 to C82 (covers); no covers relation is proposed for C99, C100 or C107, to avoid counting pure repetition twice. A1 may add covers relations for them.

## Points of tension in the text (no relation proposed)
- C105 says Housing First was scaled up "relatively quickly"; s.4.1 (p.37) says "Overall levels of recruitment were slower than had been anticipated" and F19 shows Edinburgh at 52% of its target. Both can hold; noted only.
- C63 says RSL commitment "increased as the effectiveness of the approach [...] became increasingly evident"; this sentence appears only in chapter conclusion 7.8 and the executive summary. The body section 7.6.5 reports variable buy-in but no increase. rests_on F60 only; the increase part is unsupported in the body text.
- C17 and C87 compare the 6% death rate with other programmes; the comparison rests on literature (footnote 81, p.51), not on a second strand.

## Transformations
- T1: F20 (Q) to F18 (fidelity ratings), crosses_strand yes.
- T2: F15/F16 (N) to F17 (costed case studies), crosses_strand no.
- Not recorded: unit cost multiplication of survey counts (F14-F16), sustainment rate calculation (F8), NDT scoring (F6). These operations stay within the N strand and their inputs are not registered findings (same treatment as HLT-C2).

## Other
- Table 9.10 (p.140) appears to swap the row labels for housing (£516,568) and police/criminal justice (£644,942) relative to Tables 9.7-9.8; the total (£1.84 million, about £23,000 per client) is unaffected. F14 uses the total only.
- Questionnaire completion was poor (80 baseline, 14% of those housed; 21 follow-up), and the authors state that survey outcomes are "indicative rather than representative" (p.7). This is a limitation stated by S1, not a finding.
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text; "[...]" marks omissions and square brackets mark inserted words in claims. Claim wording is otherwise the authors', with the first letter capitalised where a claim starts mid-sentence.
